text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police sting against suspected illegal arms dealers expected to shed light on last week's murder of 38-year-old father of four in Limassol.
- National Council on Cyprus issue expected to take final decisions on revised U.N. document to be discussed at second round of talks in mid-August.
- National Council backs second round of talks. Foreign Minister Cassoulides and Attorney-general Markides go to Athens on Friday for further consultations with Greek government.

- Communist Akel party chief Demetris Christofias renews appeals to centre-left United Democrats to decide now on backing presidential candidate Marios Eliades. United Democrats insist on taking final stand at end of August.
- Greek Cypriot side will finally go to Switzerland talks, making announcement pre-emptively in view of uncertainties surrounding whether Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash will attend.
- Fate of "Coalition of Hope" of opposition parties lies in hands of Akel. Last-ditch attempts to overcome differences among leaders of three parties which are members failed to yield results.
- Two architects take Central Bank of Cyprus to court, claiming it owes them 800,000 pounds ($1.5 million) from construction of a building.
